surfaces.part: gray header cap with white oval label

answer.evidence: The sign is a vertical board seen face-on. The header (rows 0-5) is a front-facing gray panel with a white label. Its width goes 8, 14, 16, then 14, so it is a flat-ended hat that steps out and back, not an ellipse. A dark outline at row 6 separates it from the board, with no front-edge line and no eave shadow below it. The brown board (rows 7-26) and the base (rows 27-30, with a dark band at row 27) are also plain vertical faces. No row range shows a horizontal top surface, so the whole drawing is a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a vertical standing sign with a brown body, a cream sign panel, a cap and a base. Measured facts: 10 visible tones per tile, against 6 (bus-shelter), 12 (kiosk) and 20 (vending) for the references, so it sits within the reference range and above bus-shelter. Near-flat coverage is 0%, and the dark edge pixels carry a tint (0% neutral), so the outline leans toward dark brown and reads as a dark material tone rather than a black sticker line. The main brown body shows about 4 steps, a little below the 5-6 on the kiosk and vending references. Texture is modest: the panel and body have some variation but little grain. It is a simple, small prop, and it does not look thinner or flatter than the accepted modern_city references, particularly the bus shelter. It is at the lower edge of the standard but acceptable.
